general_rules: Inspect under documented agreement and applicable SOP; never replace a qualified inspector or perform unsafe testing.
Document material observed defects and serious potential hazards; communicate promptly per company safety protocol.
Separate symptom from mechanism, cause hypothesis, hidden conditions and legally adopted requirements.
Unobserved and inaccessible are not defect-free; coverage gaps belong in internal ledger and material limitations in report.
Do not state code violation, code compliance, or recall confirmation without exact authenticated applicability receipts.
Do not promise zero defects, safety warranty, future service life, insurance, purchase advice, or legal immunity.
Recommend licensed or qualified specialists when evidence cannot resolve safety, structural, electrical, combustion, water or other material risk.

Customer report should be readable: location + observed condition + significance + recommended evaluation/action + material limitation. Internal hypotheses stay internal unless verified and materially useful.
Urgent warnings are not suppressed merely because a root cause is unknown; report the observed hazard with calibrated language and human escalation.
Commercial PCA must use separate agreed scope and qualified assessor; E2018 is an optional framework and is not home SOP.

unmapped_sop_topics: 3.8 Fireplace: no dedicated specialized system in current 13-system engine; required explicit scope triage
Additional smoke/CO-alarm observations and related limitations must be individually reviewed

separate_obligations: Occupancy and use, accessibility, life-safety systems, fire suppression, roof, building envelope, structural, MEP and relevant site systems require agreed PCA scope
Do not substitute ASTM E2018 for an AHJ compliance inspection, Phase I environmental assessment, or engineering report

sources.use_limit: Scope of visual residential inspection, material defects and reporting of observed concerns; contract and credentials must determine actual governing SOP.
ASHI current SOP; use direct official current text and inspector agreement to confirm exact edition.
New ASHI SOP approved January 2026; implementation listed January 1, 2027. Not active on this snapshot date.
Baseline property condition assessment of commercial property; purchased/contract-adopted standard not reproduced and not synonymous with a residential SOP.
Michigan lists state codes by discipline and edition; verify permit era, AHJ, local amendments and applicability before asserting any violation.
July 2025 injunction affects proposed residential and energy updates; verify current status for each inspection date.
Acts, rules, licensing and construction-code amendments; this list is not legal applicability proof.
Public recall API; confirm exact model, production/serial range and recall remedy directly; brand resemblance cannot prove recall.
Radon cannot be inferred visually; qualified testing and lab/device receipts required before stating measured levels.

sources.use_limit: Carbon monoxide has no detectable color or odor; visible vent concern is a reason to refer, not proof of CO level.
Model-code history and adoption context; local adopted text and amendments govern, not generic model editions.
Manufacture date code has repeating cycle; serial alone does not establish installation age.
Use only product-series-appropriate date format and original plate; serial does not establish installation date.
Warranty/model support cannot alone verify installation date or remaining life.

systems.inspection_focus: Check grading, discharge patterns and retaining features without diagnosing subsurface drainage.
systems.possible_mechanism: Negative surface grading or blocked runoff path
systems.alternative_explanation: Overflow from roof drainage or seasonal high groundwater
systems.what_would_distinguish: Observe drainage during precipitation; measure surface slope; trace roof discharge
systems.serious_warning_cue: Concentrated water reaching foundation or pedestrian ice hazard
systems.qualified_referral: Drainage / grading contractor or licensed civil engineer if significant movement.

systems.inspection_focus: Seek displacement, cracking patterns, dampness and support distress; distinguish shrinkage from possible movement.
systems.example_sign: Crack or displacement on accessible foundation face
systems.what_would_distinguish: Measure crack width and displacement; inspect drainage, history and structural load path; refer if movement suspected
systems.serious_warning_cue: Significant displacement, instability or active water entry
systems.qualified_referral: Licensed structural engineer for displacement or suspected structural failure.

systems.inspection_focus: Inspect safely visible joists, supports, moisture effects, penetrations and changes in floor plane.
systems.example_sign: Uneven, sagging or moisture-marked floor surface
systems.alternative_explanation: Span, load, foundation settlement or earlier repairs
systems.what_would_distinguish: Inspect accessible underside, member condition, moisture readings and load paths
systems.serious_warning_cue: Unsupported or visibly failing floor platform
systems.qualified_referral: Licensed structural engineer or qualified framing contractor.

systems.inspection_focus: Inspect exposed framing and connection conditions, not covered members or structural capacity.
systems.example_sign: Visible bowed or altered member at accessible framing
systems.alternative_explanation: Nonstructural irregularity, prior modification or moisture damage
systems.what_would_distinguish: Confirm member size, span, connections, loading and alteration record with qualified professional
systems.serious_warning_cue: Cracked load-bearing member or visibly compromised connection
systems.qualified_referral: Licensed structural engineer where load path or deformation is uncertain.

systems.inspection_focus: Check cladding clearances, penetration flashings, exterior openings and moisture pathways.
systems.example_sign: Staining, cracking or separation near cladding and openings
systems.alternative_explanation: Surface condensation or non-active legacy staining
systems.what_would_distinguish: Trace flashing and drainage-plane details where safely visible; moisture meter and targeted noninvasive evaluation
systems.serious_warning_cue: Loose facade components or ongoing water entry
systems.qualified_referral: Qualified building-envelope specialist or appropriate contractor.

systems.inspection_focus: Assess accessible roof-covering indications, flashings, drainage and leak evidence; do not claim remaining life.
systems.example_sign: Staining, damaged covering or ponding on visible roof area
systems.possible_mechanism: Age-related material distress or poor water shedding
systems.alternative_explanation: Storm damage, condensation or debris blockage
systems.what_would_distinguish: Document drainage/flashings from safe vantage; review leak history and attic underside where accessible
systems.serious_warning_cue: Active leakage or apparent collapse risk; avoid unsafe roof access
systems.qualified_referral: Qualified roofing contractor; structural engineer if roof structure appears compromised.

systems.inspection_focus: Note insulation, ventilation, staining, roof framing visibility and access limitations.
systems.example_sign: Discoloration, dampness or condensation on accessible attic material
systems.alternative_explanation: Roof covering leak, plumbing vent leakage or past inactive damage
systems.what_would_distinguish: Measure moisture and humidity, observe vent terminations, compare weather history
systems.serious_warning_cue: Electrical hazard near wet materials or visibly unstable roof framing
systems.qualified_referral: Qualified roofer, insulation/ventilation contractor, or engineer as applicable.

systems.inspection_focus: Look for moisture staining, egress limitations, step/guard issues, windows and doors.
systems.example_sign: Localized wall, ceiling or flooring stain/crack
systems.alternative_explanation: Plumbing source, condensation or historic repaired event
systems.what_would_distinguish: Review adjacent rooms/above/below, moisture readings and leak history
systems.serious_warning_cue: Active water near electrical, failing stairs or unsafe guarding
systems.qualified_referral: Qualified carpenter/contractor; licensed structural engineer for suspected support issue.

systems.inspection_focus: Look for readily observable panel/receptacle hazards; never open energized parts or imply tested operation.
systems.example_sign: Exposed conductor, heat marks or panel corrosion where visible
systems.possible_mechanism: Damaged wiring, loose termination or water exposure
systems.alternative_explanation: Surface dirt, labeling issue or pre-existing non-active staining
systems.what_would_distinguish: Qualified electrician to inspect de-energized condition and test as appropriate; do not open energized components
systems.serious_warning_cue: Arcing, hot equipment, damaged insulation or exposed live parts
systems.qualified_referral: Licensed electrician; advise prompt safety evaluation of exposed conductors or heat damage.

systems.inspection_focus: Look for leaks, corrosion, visible drain and supply characteristics, fixture behavior when tested.
systems.example_sign: Moisture and corrosion near accessible joint
systems.what_would_distinguish: Observe under operating conditions when safe, meter moisture, trace water source
systems.serious_warning_cue: Active uncontrolled leak or contaminated wastewater
systems.qualified_referral: Licensed plumber for leaking, unsafe or unverified systems.

systems.inspection_focus: Check accessible venting, leakage, corrosion, relief arrangement and rating plate; no date from appearance.
systems.example_sign: Rust, water trace or soot around water heater
systems.what_would_distinguish: Verify exact product/venting instructions and operating checks by qualified technician
systems.serious_warning_cue: Potential combustion-gas hazard, apparent unsafe venting or active leak
systems.qualified_referral: Licensed plumber or qualified HVAC technician for vent/combustion hazards.

systems.inspection_focus: Record system identification, visible flue, condensate, distribution and observed operation only when actually tested.
systems.example_sign: Corrosion, water pooling or irregular vent termination
systems.alternative_explanation: Normal defrost drainage, inactive history or adjacent plumbing
systems.what_would_distinguish: Review model-specific manufacturer instructions; qualified HVAC operational testing
systems.serious_warning_cue: Suspected combustion exhaust exposure or damaged gas piping
systems.qualified_referral: Licensed HVAC professional; CO concern is not visually diagnosable.

systems.inspection_focus: Assess safely accessible moisture, vapor control, supports and concealed-area limits.
systems.example_sign: Wet soil, stained members or displaced supports
systems.possible_mechanism: Ground moisture intrusion or poor vapor control
systems.alternative_explanation: Plumbing leak, surface runoff or seasonal flood history
systems.what_would_distinguish: Moisture mapping, observe source routes, assess support geometry and access limitations
systems.serious_warning_cue: Visible structural instability, active flooding or suspected biological hazard
systems.qualified_referral: Crawlspace/moisture specialist and structural engineer where warranted.
